description: The whole installation at a glance: every account, every service. Filters use the index labels service_name, deployment_environment, account_id and event_category; the event type, the actor and the object are Loki structured metadata. Click an account in the Top accounts table to drill down into the Account activity dashboard.

panels.description: All events of the selected services, environments, accounts and categories over the dashboard time range.
panels.title: Events

panels.description: Accounts that produced at least one event over the time range.
panels.title: Active accounts

panels.description: Distinct users (actor_type = user) behind the events over the time range. API keys, guests and system actions are not counted.

targets.expr: count(sum by (actor_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id", event_category=~"$category"} | actor_type="user" [$__range])))

panels.title: Active users

panels.description: user.login events over the time range.
panels.title: Sign-ins

panels.description: user.login_failed events over the time range. Red as soon as there is one; the Security row below shows where they come from.
panels.title: Failed sign-ins

panels.description: workflow.run events over the time range.
panels.title: Workflows started

panels.description: task.complete events over the time range.
panels.title: Tasks completed

panels.description: file.access_denied events over the time range: the backend refused a file download. Red as soon as there is one.
panels.title: Refused downloads

panels.description: Number of events per category in each time bucket, all accounts together.
panels.title: Events by category

panels.description: Number of events per account in each time bucket. Pick an account in the Account variable, or open the Account activity dashboard from the Top accounts table, to see one of them alone.
panels.title: Events by account

panels.description: Backend events against file service events in each time bucket.
panels.title: Events by service

panels.description: Fifteen most active accounts over the time range. Click an account id to open its Account activity dashboard with the same time range.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (account_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id", event_category=~"$category"} [$__range])))

panels.title: Top accounts

panels.description: Fifteen most frequent event types over the time range, all accounts together.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (event_type) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id", event_category=~"$category"} [$__range])))

panels.title: Top event types

panels.description: Who produces the events: people in the browser (user), integrations (api_key), guest links (guest) and the system itself (system).
panels.title: Events by actor type

panels.description: Authentication events in each time bucket, all accounts together.
panels.title: Sign-ins, failures, sign-outs, sign-ups

panels.description: Fifteen most active users over the time range with their account. Backend records only: the file service names a user by id without the e-mail, its traffic per account is in the Files row.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (account_id, actor_id, pii_actor_email) (count_over_time({service_name="pneumatic-backend", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id", event_category=~"$category"} | actor_type="user" [$__range])))

panels.title: Top users

panels.description: Ten addresses with the most user.login_failed events over the time range and the reason the backend gave. A failed sign-in has no actor; the e-mail is stored hashed only.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (pii_ip, payload_reason) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id"} | event_type="user.login_failed" [$__range])))

panels.title: Failed sign-ins by source

panels.description: user.login_as (a superuser signed in as a user) and tenant.login_as (a master account signed in as a tenant), newest first. Every one of them is a deliberate act worth a look.
panels.title: Staff sign-ins on behalf of users and tenants

panels.description: Changes that widen or narrow access, newest first: API keys, admin rights, deactivations, groups, webhook subscriptions, deleted templates and workflows.
panels.title: Account administration

panels.description: Workflow lifecycle events in each time bucket, all accounts together.
panels.title: Workflows

panels.description: Task events in each time bucket, all accounts together.
panels.title: Tasks

panels.description: Template events in each time bucket, all accounts together.
panels.title: Templates

panels.description: Records of the file service in each time bucket: file.upload, file.download (one per download, the ranges a player asks for afterwards are the same download) and file.access_denied (the backend refused the download).
panels.title: Uploads, downloads, refusals

panels.description: Sum of the file sizes (payload.size) of the uploads and of the downloads over the time range.
panels.title: Bytes uploaded and downloaded

panels.description: Ten accounts with the largest sum of uploaded and downloaded bytes over the time range.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (account_id) (sum_over_time({service_name="pneumatic-file-service", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id"} | event_type=~"file.upload|file.download" | unwrap payload_size | __error__="" [$__range])))
